The Japanese Department of the Communists in Shanghai.
Secretary Comrade Kawakani,
Comrade Secretary,
6614
24.9.26

Leaving the Far East I consider it my duty to express to you
and to all those members of the Shanghai Japanese Communist
Association my sincere thanks for the very productive work in which
you indulge goin hand-in-hand with the proletariat of the U.S.S.R.
I thank you all in the name of the Proletariat and wish you all
complete success in your productive work and hope you will not
forget it, notwithstanding any obstacles which are created against
us by the agents of the capitalists. I know very well and love
beautiful Japan and the people of Japan but it hurts terribly to
see that the people of Japan haven't got the chance of enjoying
all the benefits of their country as anywhere where there are
followers of Imperialists they oppress and vilify them in gaols and
in their torture cells hundreds and thousands of innocent poor
people dead and the poor people who are fighting for the rights of
humanity and help of their comrades where every step and every
word of a workman is controlled by well fed and snobbish rascals
and blackguards(?) who are building their own prosperity in the
blood of the proletariat. Don't neglect Comrades your work and
don't be disappointed in the failures and obstacles. Go ahead with
courage and pave your hard and terrible road and you will be
appreciated later by your people and they will give you their
thanks. I think an awful lot of the work of Comrade Kuwakami
and his work will be reported by me in detail to my Government.
Once again I thank you etc., and repeat, be courageous comrades
and go ahead, the wonderful bright sun of splendid free Japan
awaits you.
To you all I send my Comrades' greeting.

President for China
Comrade Karakhan
25/8/25.

U S S R
R K P
Peking

6614
24. 9. 25
Shanghai Municipal Police

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL）
DIRECTOR OF CRIMINAL
INTELLIGENCE

Shanghai, September 18, 1925.

Sir,

K. Kawakami who is referred to in attached
document, which is of somewhat doubtful authenticity,
is well known as one of the principal members of the
Japanese Communist party in Shanghai. His photograph is
attached. He was connected with the teaching staff of
the Hsin Hwa Esperanto School at 1789 North Szechuen
Road which occupied our serious attention for some
considerable time as it served as a rendez-vous for the
Russian, Korean, Japanese and Chinese Communists of
shanghai.

One of the leaders of Esperanto at that place,
a Mr. Stopani, committed suicide. Kawakami was a
friend of his and he guided around Shanghai the blind
Russian Communist poet Yeroshenko, who visited the
school and had himself photographed with the members
of its staff.

Your Obedient Servant,
McLaughlin
D. C. I.

Commissioner of police.
